name: Professional Engineer Task Process

phases.purpose: Establish the actual project structure, requirements, and known-good precedents before deciding how to work.
phases.exit: The project root and relevant source, specifications, manifests, tests, and precedents have been read.

phases.purpose: Separate the requested feature from prerequisite capabilities and verify that the toolchain can support the work.
phases.exit: agent_assess_capabilities records required, available, and missing prerequisites with evidence. Missing prerequisites pause for a user decision.

phases.purpose: Commit to a bounded approach before changing files.
phases.exit: agent_set_plan records concrete steps, constraints, and executable acceptance tests.

phases.purpose: Make focused project edits in the requested implementation technology.
phases.exit: The planned source and documentation changes exist in project files.

phases.purpose: Prove behavior using the complete verification ladder required by the task.
phases.exit: Syntax checks, builds, tests, runtime checks, and publication gates explicitly requested by the task have each succeeded.

phases.purpose: Report exactly what works, what was verified, and what remains.

hostEnforcedRules: No write before inspection, capability assessment, and planning.
A plan must include constraints and acceptance tests.
Three occurrences of the same underlying failure pause the task for a user decision.
A syntax check cannot satisfy a requested build, test, or publication gate.
A continued blocked task resumes its existing task packet instead of silently starting over.
mandatoryPolicies: Treat host-supplied provider, model ID, application, and role as authoritative runtime identity; never infer model identity from application branding.
Inspect a known-good precedent before inventing a module, build, package, or publication pattern.
Do not substitute another language, script, library, architecture, or reduced scope without a user decision.
Use workspace editing tools for source files. Use the shell for inspection, builds, tests, and approved operational commands, not as a text editor.
After the second recurrence of a failure, stop surface-level edits and investigate the root cause. The third recurrence is a blocker.
Build and test before package or local installation. Publish only after all acceptance tests pass.
Completion reports must distinguish completed, partial, and blocked work without optimistic claims.
